Desaire diplomático en México 🇲🇽👑 La reina Rania de Jordania  de origen palestino  visitó México  el pasado 5 de septiembre para participar en el foro México Siglo XXI en el WTC de la CDMX. Ahí denunció las acciones de Israel contra Gaza y elogió a la mujer mexicana por su fuerza y liderazgo  ganándose la ovación de miles de jóvenes universitarios.

Lo polémico vino después ni la presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum ni el canciller Juan Ramón de la Fuente sostuvieron un encuentro oficial con la monarca. En protocolo diplomático  debieron recibirla en Palacio Nacional o Cancillería  pero no ocurrió.
Aunque no haya sido “visita de Estado”  el hecho de que la reina Rania asistiera a un foro público en México y hablara de temas sensibles (como Palestina y Gaza) implica una relevancia política y simbólica. Por eso se considera apropiado y hasta necesario un gesto oficial de recepción  aunque fuese discreto.
Analistas consideran que se trató de una falta de coordinación en la agenda oficial  lo que terminó viéndose como un silencio diplomático y un desaire hacia una de las mujeres más influyentes del mundo árabe. Para muchos  fue una oportunidad perdida de reforzar los lazos entre México y Jordania.

Te dejo estos dos gestos. Parece el mismo  pero no lo es. Se trata del código conocido por la ciencia del comportamiento humano como UA29L y UA29R (desplazamiento a la izquierda (Left) o derecha (Right)  por sus siglas en inglés. 

El gesto -siempre que no existan razones fisiológicas  patológicas o de tics preexistentes- está asociado a emociones de valencia negativa tales como la frustración o ira en el contexto de la reflexión  análisis o duda. 

En el segundo caso  los dientes quedan expuestos del mismo modo que lo hacen otros mamiferos como los gatos o los perros  para mostrar no solo ira  sino la disposición al ataque. 

Si en una conversación tu interlocutor  mueve la mandíbula de izquiera a derecha  es una señal de que las cosas no están bien y que se avecina una discusión. Si  además se ven sus dientes  preparate para afrontar un desacuerdo activo en una probable discusión acalorada. 

Ambos gestos generalmente aparecen de forma más sutil. Los he exagerado un poco para que puedas apreciarlos. Casi siempre aparecen acompañados de un suspiro o resoplido (diferenciador)

Hoy nos toca compartir una noticia triste que golpea a México 🖤. Hace unas horas explotó una pipa de gas LP en la Calzada Zaragoza  bajo el Puente de la Concordia en Iztapalapa (CDMX)  dejando una escena devastadora con múltiples heridos  autos atrapados y lamentablemente ya varias víctimas mortales.

📌 Lo que se sabe hasta el momento:
	•	El incendio fue controlado 5.30 pm  pero dejó más de 70 lesionados y al menos 4 personas fallecidas.
	•	20 de los heridos fueron trasladados en estado grave a diferentes hospitales.
	•	El jefe de gobierno Martí Batres informó que 3 personas permanecen muy graves en terapia intensiva.
	•	La presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum y autoridades federales expresaron solidaridad con las familias de las víctimas y reconocimiento a los cuerpos de emergencia.

Hoy más que nunca recordamos que detrás de estos hechos hay familias  amigos y sueños que se apagan de manera injusta. Más allá de llamarlo accidente  también debemos cuestionarnos la negligencia y exigir mayor seguridad en este tipo de transportes  para que tragedias así no se repitan.

Desde Puebla  la familia de Sandungueo Show  mandamos fuerza  abrazo y solidaridad a todas las personas afectadas 🙏🕊️.

La Catedral de la Ciudad de México se asienta sobre arcillas blandas y rellenos históricos  y es por eso que hoy se hunde de forma desigual.

Las construcciones prehispánicas y coloniales comprimieron algunas áreas del subsuelo  endureciéndolas  mientras que otras zonas  sin tanta carga histórica  quedaron más blandas y hundibles. 

A lo largo de siglos  la inclinación se ha acumulado: en algunos puntos las columnas tienen hasta 90 cm más de altura que en otros  para compensar los desniveles. 

La sobreexplotación del agua en Ciudad de México hunde el suelo cada vez más rápido: hoy  la Catedral se hunde a un ritmo de aproximadamente 7.4 cm al año  más del doble que en 1970.

Si sigue así  en 100 años el desequilibrio sería catastrófico.

Te explicamos cómo es este proceso  que se replica en otras zonas de la CDMX.

Del Fuerte  empresa mexicana dedicada a la producción de derivados del tomate  fue fundada en 1928 en el Valle del Río Fuerte  en Sinaloa. Los fundadores fueron un grupo de visionarios agricultores y empresarios locales  liderados por Rafael Buelna Tenorio  un hombre que combatió en la Revolución Mexicana  apasionado por el desarrollo agrícola de la región. Buelna  originario de Sinaloa  impulsó la iniciativa para industrializar la producción de tomates  aprovechando la fertilidad de la zona. En 1945  la empresa se trasladó a la ex-hacienda La Corona en Culiacán  Sinaloa  consolidando su operación bajo la visión de estos pioneros que enfatizaban la calidad natural y el orgullo mexicano. Comparto un anuncio televisivo de la década de los 50  cuando un recurso muy usado fue la animación para hacer destacar los productos y las marcas  dentro de gusto de las familias mexicanas!

Las ciudades se reconfiguran: entre mapas redibujados y desplazamientos. 🌇 ⁠
⁠
Sabemos que el tiempo en el tráfico nos cuesta mucho más que paciencia: las personas pierden horas y horas atrapadas en la congestión vehicular  en el mejor de los casos. 🚕 🚗 🚒⁠
⁠
Si consideramos que muchas de las soluciones tradicionales—como añadir más transporte público o poner más segundos pisos—no logran aliviar ese caos  cabe preguntarse: ¿y si en lugar de optimizar el movimiento  replanteamos el territorio donde vivimos? 🤔⁠
⁠
En otros países  el concepto de ciudades policéntricas ha demostrado reducir tiempos de traslado y mejorar la calidad de vida. En México  hemos transitado hacia algo semejante desde los ochenta  cuando se inició una descentralización industrial con las ciudades satélite. ☝️⁠
⁠
Ese viraje permitió que  gradualmente  no todo el empleo ni los servicios estuvieran concentrados en el corazón de la capital  abriendo nuevos polos alrededor de ella. 🙌⁠
⁠
Esto nos recuerda que descentralizar no sólo implica trasladar desarrollo  sino planificar con responsabilidad esas nuevas zonas de vida. ✨⁠
⁠
Quizá se trate de redibujar el territorio desde lo cotidiano  para que el destino no sea una ruta agotadora  sino una vida cercana y más tranquila. 💥 ⁠

Sharing My Disappointing Weekend in Mexico City – Just My Experience . Let me start by saying this is just my personal opinion and experience  I m not here to bash anyone s favorite place I just want to share my honest take in hopes that it helps others when planning a trip  For context  I m from Los Angeles and consider myself a fairly seasoned traveler   I recently took a weekend trip to Mexico City  planned Thursday to Monday   Our flight landed Thursday afternoon  and we checked into our hotel which was actually great  That night  we had dinner at Café Madre and then did a little taco tour  Unfortunately  the following morning  my partner woke up with Montezuma s Revenge  Thankfully  we had anticipated the risk and packed all the right meds   After a slow morning  we headed to Contramar for lunch  We had the tuna tostadas and the famous flatted fish both were just okay  Honestly  we ve had better versions elsewhere  but we brushed it off  That night  we went to Handshake and had a great experience there  However  once we got back to the hotel  I couldn t sleep and then it hit me  awful stomach cramps  body aches the whole thing  I was completely out of commission all Saturday   My partner  luckily feeling a bit better  explored the city while I stayed in  She brought back pastries that everyone had hyped up again  just okay  Later  she tried to go back out but ended up returning early as her symptoms came back   We re staying in Roma Norte  and one thing we really noticed is how not pedestrian friendly the city feels  Cars rarely yield for people  a lot of traffic lights don t work  and crossing the street always feels like a gamble  It honestly makes getting around on foot kind of exhausting and stressful   So far  the food here has been just okay and it s frustrating having to constantly calculate where  or if  you should eat because you don t want to risk getting sick again   Our flight was originally scheduled for Monday morning  but out of frustration and not feeling well  we decided to cut the trip short and rebooked for Sunday afternoon  It just didn t feel worth it to push through another day feeling sick and underwhelmed   All in all  it s been a frustrating experience  I know people love CDMX  and I m sure there s lots to love here  but this was our experience and unfortunately  it just didn t live up to the hype   We re fresh from a recent trip to Hong Kong and are closing our eyes imagining we re there right now   ___________________________________________  EDIT  Lab results came back  it was ecoli    We made sure to take all of the proper precautions   Brushed teeth with bottled water  mouth closed in shower  drink only bottled water  no raw vegetables   Additionally  we crossed referenced every place we went to with Reddit  Google  and blogs to make sure we would be in the clear  Bad luck        We have a med bag wherever we go  and alter the contents depending on the destination  Thankfully  we were as prepared as we could ve been for this situation so make sure you do the same  Had tons of electrolyte packets    I posted this knowing I would be downvoted to hell  but it s so important that experiences like this be prevalent in a travel community just as much as the positive ones IMO  Not trying to turn anybody off of the destination  but just be careful

Mexico Trip Report (2 months, mid-range budget, 3 states - full itinerary & cost.) . 63 days  15 accommodations  9 cities    towns   8 busses  6 flights    My wife and I just spent 2 months travelling to and around Mexico from New Zealand  I used this subreddit A LOT for advice and planning so I wanted to contribute my experience for future travellers  but also challenge some common views about travelling in Mexico  especially from this sub  Some financial stuff at the end   I firstly just want to say that overall throughout the whole country we felt incredibly safe at all times  We were never threatened  never scammed  We walked streets at night  drank in bars  rode public transport  swam in lakes  lagoons  cenotes and oceans  ate street food  rented motorbikes and cars  went to remote areas  and drove at night  We never felt unsafe  weren t targeted by police  and generally just had a wonderful time  It s worth noting that we are highly experienced travellers in our late 30 s  and with that experience and age comes a fair amount of travel instinct to avoid bad dangerous situations  However  from our experience I wouldn t say that the places we visited in Mexico are any more or less dangerous than any other country I ve been to    We barely spoke rudimentary Spanish  just the most basic phrases  but we did try which we felt gave us an advantage  We work while travelling and as such we chose to stay mostly in apartments using AirBnb  as hotel rooms are too small for travelling and working for this long  Everything was private  no shared rooms apartments etc   and what we would consider mid range  Oh  and the WiFi everywhere we went  even tiny beach towns  was fast and reliable     Mexico City   15 nights       Auckland to CDMX via LAX  Hotel on arrival  AirBnb for 7 nights in Moderna  AirBnb for 7 nights in Narvarte     Mexico City is huge and awesome  Street food is everywhere  it s cheap and delicious  Taxis are cheap  Uber   trains and buses are even cheaper and are reliable  We spent most of our time around Roma  Condesa and Centro but didn t stay there  We broke up our accommodation to experience different areas  but also to not gamble on just one apartment for two weeks  Teotihuacan and Xochimilco are worthy day trips  Coyoacan is also worth a whole day or more  If I were to return I d definitely just pay a bit more to stay in Roma  We loved exploring other areas  but Roma and Condesa are where we felt compelled to return     Guanajuato   3 nights      Bus from CDMX to Guanajuato  ETN Buses  5 5 hours  AirBnb in San Clemente    Guanajuato has a really cool vibe and is one of the most beautiful towns I ve ever been to  It feels straight out of Europe  You can walk everywhere   take a night walking tour that tells the love story with a live band  it s awesome even if you don t speak Spanish  There s not a lot to do but eat  drink and take in the view  There s a mummy museum but we didn t go     San Miguel de Allende   2 nights      Bus from Guanajuato to SMDE  ETN Buses  1 5 hours  AirBnb in Centro    San Miguel de Allende is also incredibly beautiful  especially at sunset  and you can walk the entire central area in an evening  For us however it was one of our least favourite places  the vibe just felt off  It felt like about 50  of the town was made up of expats  retirees  and we didn t feel very welcome from locals  It s worth a night if you re in the area  but I wouldn t go out of my way to go there     Puebla   3 nights      Bus from SMDE to Pubela  ETN Buses  6 hours  Airbnb in Centro    Puebla is cooler than I expected  The food is really good  Centro is walkable and has a cool vibe  We visited Puebla but  although cool  we felt it was overhyped and tourist focused  Find the raisin liqueur spot      Oaxaca   10 nights       Bus from Puebla to Oacaxa  ADO buses  4 5 hours  Hotel on arrival  Airbnb for 9 nights in Xochimilco La Cascada    Oaxaca was easily our favourite place in Mexico  It s a medium sized city but feels like a small town  The food is absolutely next level and entirely lives up to the hype  We drank a lot of Mezcal  took a Mezcal tour and really soaked it in  The art   textiles are also amazing  From our AirBnb we were able to walk the whole centro area  which is pretty much where we spent all our time  Monte Alban was awesome and totally worth it   Hierve el Agua  was also really cool  Definitely visit a Mezcal distillery and budget a bit extra for food  and take a walking tour     Puerto Escondido   5 nights       Bus   transit van  from Oaxaca to PE  Ruta Coatlanes  3 5 hours  AirBnb in Los Mangos    Puerto Escondido the town itself is kind of average  but it has a bunch of cool beaches with clubs   restaurants  The Zicaleta area is more of a vibe and we d probably stay there if we returned  but it s easy enough to rent a scooter and just ride around  We spent every day just relaxing on beaches  swimming  drinking cocktails and eating ceviche  We also spent one day at a nice beach club which was totally worth it  We did do a bioluminescent tour  which was amazing  but we didn t realise that the lagoon you swim in is actually inhabited by crocodiles  Spanish only tour   so heads up there     Mazunte   5 nights      Bus from PE to San Antonio  1 hour   Taxi from SA to Mazunte  15 mins   AirBnb    Mazunte is a really cool little beach town with a super chill hippy vibe  There are a lot of travellers and expats  so the local culture is thin  but coming from a similar town in NZ ourselves  we actually just felt at home  Mazunte had the best swimming of our whole trip  We rented an ATV and explored Zipolite and San Augustinillo  but Mazunte was the best  Definitely take a dolphin boat tour   we saw dolphins  turtles and a whale  Accommodation here is a real indoor outdoor style      Oaxaca   1 night     Bus from Mazunte to PE  then from PE to Oaxaca  Hotel    Another night in Oaxaca to fly to Merida     Merida   7 nights      Flight from Oaxaca to Merida  Volaris  1 5 hours  AirBnb in Garcia Gineres    Merida is fine  but really it s all about the surrounding areas  We rented a car with Yucatan Rentals  highly recommended  for our whole Yucatan stay and drove everywhere ourselves  Seriously  our trip wouldn t have been the same without our own car  Temperatures were in the mid 40 s  celcius  and having to bus taxi tuktuk around to the beaches and cenotes would have been hell  We visited 9 cenotes  Uxmal  Progresso  and the whole Progresso to Xtampu coast  Driving allowed us to stop in small towns and visit less touristy cenotes  which really enhanced our experience  We also visited Izamal but didn t think it was worth it     Valladolid   4 nights      Drive from Merida to Valladolid 2 5 hours  Apartment in Sisal via Booking com    Valladolid is a beautiful little town  easily walkable  aside from the heat   There s a convent where they show the town s history each night on the walls  We found the food really good in the whole region  but specifically here  We drove up to Rio Lagartos and took a mangrove tour which I d highly recommend  We saw crocodiles and thousands of Flamingos  saw the salt flats  took a  Mayan bath   and swam at a beautiful private beach      Merida   3 nights      Drive from Valladolid to Merida 2 5 hours  AirBnb in Centro    Back to Merida for a few nights  where we booked a place with a pool and just chilled for a few days     Mexico City   3 nights      Flight from Merida to Mexico City  Aero Mexico  2 5 hours  Airbnb in Condesa    Back to spend a few more days in CDMX before flying home  Lots of shopping  walking around eating   drinking and just soaking up the city atmosphere     CDMX to Auckland via LAX                                        Costs  NZD     NZ to Mexico flight    4767  Internal flights    955  Internal buses    673  Rental Car    771  Motorbike Rentals    300  Petrol    300  Accommodation total    5620  Travel insurance    781  I think  very roughly  we spent about  120    140 NZD per day on everything else not listed above  Food  drinks  activities  local transport  tours etc  So all up for a 2 month trip for 2 people we spent about  22k NZD  We saved for about 16 months  and also earned while we were there to achieve this on very moderate incomes                                      Final Thoughts    Mexico is incredible  and it was one of the best places we ve been  The food  history  art  music and people are all amazing    Much of the advice we read online was very conservative and cautious  and while I would always advise common sense while travelling  be aware that most people travelling in Mexico have safe  wonderful experiences  and therefore most of the time don t feel the need to write reviews or post on Reddit  As a result  much of what you read is overly cautious and negative    Yes there is trouble in parts of Mexico  Yes the sanitation is a bit different  Yes you might get a bit sick eating street food  Yes you need to be careful going out drinking  and keep your wits about you  Yes you might overpay for some food or a souvenir every now and then  You should definitely keep away from drugs  prostitution  and dark alleys in bad neighbourhoods  But these points also apply to travelling in most of the rest of the world  Use your common sense  be respectful and kind  relax  and you ll be Mexico 🇲🇽 Trip Report . I just got back from my first time  two week trip to Mexico where I stayed in CDMX and Puerto Vallarta with my SO  I flew from London Heathrow and split my time equally between the two cities    This community has been instrumental in helping me plan my travels so I thought I d give something back in return   Cash  If you re from the UK  chances are none of the Banorte ATMs will work for you  none did in my case  Citibanamex ATMs on the other hand always worked flawlessly  If you like street food and plan on buying stuff from the numerous flea markets I d suggest around MXN 1000 pp per day    Language  Mexico is obviously a Spanish speaking country so knowing some basic  Duolingo level Spanish will go a long way in making your life easier  I got by fine with a vocabulary of around 50 words although translation apps came in handy often  If you do rely on apps  make sure to download the two languages that you ll be translating between e g English and Spanish as most apps rely on the internet to work   What I was surprised by was the fact that about 10 out of the 12 members of airport staff I interacted with  none of them spoke English  in the country s main international airport mind you    Staff at the British Airways counter were great but everywhere else  especially VivaAero was none existent  In Puerto Vallarta  there were a lot more English speaking staff   Getting Around  I found both CDMX and PV extremely walkable but Uber was amazing in both cities and a lot cheaper than in the UK  All drivers were polite and kept their vehicles clean  I kept reading conflicting reports on using Uber at Mexican airports but in my experience no issues whatsoever at CDMX  was picked up and dropped off right in front of the terminal   In PV Uber dropped me off right in front of the terminal too however when the came to pick me up and take me to the city centre I had to cross the white pedestrian bridge and take it from there  If you have mobility problems and lots of luggage that bridge might be a challenge in that case just get an official taxi   Food  AMAZING  Street food  family restaurants  gourmet places were all amazing  If you re the only foreigner in the queue that s probably a good sign  In PV I really enjoyed Joe Jack s  Tuna Azul and Vicky  the seafood lady on the beach in Zona Romántica    From CDMX Villa Maria was by far the most memorable place for me  totally worth the money   Tipping  Tipping is absolutely ridiculous  I mean I can understand tipping at a restaurant or a cafeteria with table service but asking for tips in souvenir shops  Taking the piss really  A minority of people expected tips even though they were shite at their job like lazy waiters that ignore you etc    Service  The majority of people were great at their jobs  from luggage handlers to receptionists and barmen  Actually  even most random people in the street were great and were keen on helping you with directions or suggestions    Safety and Homelessness  Compared to major European cities  there were a lot less homeless people in the city centres and the few ones I saw were not aggressive or annoying  I never felt unsafe walking late at night with my SO but then again I m a big guy and maybe got lucky  Just be aware of your surroundings just like you should be anywhere you go   Beaches  In PV I only got to visit the beaches  at San Pancho  Yelapa  Quimixto and Los Muertos  If you re looking for crystal clear water you won t find that in any of those  The water has a kind of green hue so there s very little visibility  This isn t to say that water is dirty  it is not  I found the overall scenery spectacular in all the above places although if you like quiet you won t find that in Los Muertos or San Pancho due to the hordes of vendors walking by the sunbeds trying to sell you stuff   Activities  Pyramids in CDMX 100   Xochimilco was meh but I m not really a party guy  In PV the dolphin swimming session was great   Mobile Data  Don t use Airalo  it worked fine for a few days and then it didn t  Just get some cash and go to an Oxxo store and get a proper SIM card    Overall  I definitely plan on visiting Mexico in the future again  hopefully with an improved Spanish vocabulary and the will to go to less touristy areas

Just back from Mexico and we survived! . Just a little tongue in cheek title due to all the friends and family who said we d be robbed  kidnapped or killed if we weren t careful  Perhaps this might be true in the beach towns but we stuck to the interior of the country and for the most part had a good time   Things I wouldn t do again Go on a tour  I discovered I am not a tour person  The regimented schedules breakfast at 7am  lack of free time and spending over a week with the same 25 Americans that extend into cliques drove me bonkers not to mention they were all at least 10 years older than me and mostly retired  I felt it really took away from any genuine experience I could have with the locals  Not to mention the dorky name pouches   Safety despite the fears and scaremongering we stuck to the tourist areas of Puebla Oaxaca CDMX and saw nothing  scary   Just families shopping  eating and young folks out in parks and making out on benches  Reminded me of Italy as everyone comes out in good weather and are in the parks and on the streets  Very different than America  There was a strong police presence every wear and almost all the cities had police posted around especially in Mexico City where there where barricades to stop protestors from gathering  Honestly  I felt more scared riding the DC Metro some days than in Mexico City  But I was always cautious and aware of the guys who stood around and stared at me  Also be aware especially in Oaxaca that there are child beggars who will ask for money our guide said NOT to give money as they are usually tied into gangs  Better to give to the various orphanages and organizations in the city   I wasn t wowed at the food except we did have two good meals  One at Las Danzantes in Oaxaca  Believe the hype as the venue food and our wonderful waiter Oscar made it 5 stars  And it was my first time trying Bohemia Obscura beer  Another good meal was at El Cardenal in CDMX old fashion Mexican cooking but my salmon with mango sauce was so tender and the mangoes actually tasted fresh  And they had the best lime margarita in my travels  Just be aware that Mexicans love this place and it s usually a 20 min wait for a table And it s not a romantic venue very loud and crowded  And fairly cheap by US standards  Also  I can recommend Los Callejeros in Centro Historico CDMX for veggie tacos but bring your Google Translate as the staff doesn t speak English well  The corn smut and squash blossom tacos were amazing  And of course  CDMX would not be complete without a trip to Pasteleria Ideal for some yummy pastries  We came in late in the morning and it was easier to see how to grab your goodies  go to the first desk and get your receipt to pay  pay at the cashiers window and then go back to get your bag  We got 3 pastries for  2 00 which is cheap for Americans  Note food workers in Mexico do NOT wear gloves  I have to admit it bothered me and I m not sure if it was a a handler or a lukewarm buffet that gave me Montezuma s revenge for three days  It was three days of hell and I felt miserable but I managed to shake it before the trip ended   I tried Pepto but the only thing that help was the Immodium AD  I will definitely travel with this again in Mexico   We stayed in Centro Historico and I don t know whether the crowds and pollution smells contributed to it but I didn t love the city as most people here do  The customer service was surly if you didn t speak Spanish we got many dirty looks when we used Google Translate  And it was just wall to wall people around our hotel on Palma  We did go into Reforma and that seemed slightly more manageable with a better variety of restaurants  The worst part was the Terminal 1 airport at MEX international airport  A bad smell and chaos through the security screening  Note perhaps it might be better for the airport to hire at least one security personnel who spoke English  as being told what to do in Spanish is not helpful for those who don t know the language   I absolutely loved Oaxaca where the shopkeepers seemed friendly and more relaxed and life wasn t quite so frentic  And our drive into the countryside showed jut how poor that area was  Very dry lots of street dogs everywhere and women in small towns making tortillas the old fashion way  I came away with more of an appreciation of the diversity of Mexico and Mexicans themselves  And how our politics on both sides of the border are striking similar both have a Trump like bloviator    Finally most Mexicans realize the rhetoric from some camps in the US is all politics They realize Trump talks about illegals for political gain not because he believes it himself  As one guide told us   Your government was able to find and kill the head of ISIS and found and killed Saddam and bin Laden in a cave  They definitely have the technology to eliminate the tunnels under the wall and stop the illegal flow into the US  but choose not to in order to stir up support for both political parties   They also know that not all Americans hate Mexicans as evidence by millions who come to vacation there every year  The ones who don t like Mexicans don t come   So while it s good to be back in familiar surroundings  I miss the constant sun and warm temps of Mexico  Also I good rule of thumb is to bring take out at least some pesos we did  2000 and paid for some meals and other small items as well as needing change for the bathrooms  Just be aware that there will always be something missing in Mexican public bathrooms  You will usually be given a small square of toilet paper  but many times there was no soap or no paper towels or hand dryer  So plan according always bring at least a rag and or soap or paper towels to wash and dry hands   Hope this in some ways help others  And I still trying
